doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Arranging A Love Supreme and deadlines
summary: His Carnegie Hall Band arrangement of Coltrane's work fell short, and he now avoids rushed deadlines.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: More recently you took on a big — it would seem like a challenge to me — with doing “A Love Supreme,” with was it the Carnegie Hall band?
The Carnegie Hall Band, yeah. I didn’t do a very good job.
Oh you’re saying that again.
Great songs. Have you listened to that CD?
Yeah.
By ‘Trane?
Yeah.
It’s a great CD.
Lord, I wouldn’t know where to start.
That’s why actually I go back and say oh my arrangement definitely didn’t make it. Because the music they played was so high on there.
Well I would agree that it would be very hard to capture that intensity. I don’t care how many guys you have.
Yeah.
Sometimes all those people can’t match what happened with those four individuals.

I was missing the point. I missed it. And what I need to do with “A Love Supreme,” I need to listen to that album for a year. Because there is so much music there that you can’t just get all of that really fast and know what’s going on there. I had to do it too fast. And when I was listening to the CD I was thinking man, this is a lot of music in here. And every time you listen to another track there’s a lot of music in there, and then there’s a lot of music all the way through the whole thing. So my arrangement wasn’t — it was a good idea but it didn’t make it.
What percentage of your own work do you feel like that about?
Well most times what’s happening was I was going too fast. Having to finish too fast.
Deadlines. Right? You’re given a deadline?

Yeah. One time before I was working — before I was working with deadlines — and deadlines are funny things. When you have a deadline you have to find out how you can arrive at that deadline with the most quality in what you’re doing. And a lot of times trying to get there fast is the worst way to go there. I found out recently when you have something that you don’t have much time to do, make sure that you’re rested first so your mind will work on the highest level that it can. And then even if you can’t spend a lot of time on it, the time that you spend you’ll be producing the best music that you can find. But if you work tired it’s going to take the quality of the music down. So that’s what I did many times when I was making deadlines. So now what I do is I take all the time that I need until I really enjoy what it is that I’m writing, I don’t put it down.
So if you got a call to do some writing and we need this next Thursday, would you most likely turn that down?
Most times I would turn it down. I would recommend somebody that I know does those deadline things very well.
